Modern Faber

Community Policy

Craft Group Internal Operating Policy

This group is designed to produce consistent, high-quality output through enforced accountability. Members ship meaningful work every week. If that stops happening, the system is failing.

1

Objective

Everything optimizes for one outcome: members ship meaningful work every week. If this is not happening, the system is failing.

2

Operating Principles

  1. Output is the only signal that matters.
  2. Consistency beats intensity.
  3. Constraints create quality.
  4. Social pressure is a feature, not a bug.
  5. Removal is necessary to maintain standards.

3

System Design

Weekly Cadence

  • Fixed weekly deadline. No rolling submissions.
  • All submissions posted before deadline.
  • No batching. No skipping weeks.

Submission Format (Strict)

[Output]

  • Link
  • 1-3 line description

[Craft]

  • What specific detail was iterated on and why

[Blocker]

  • Where progress slowed or failed

No deviation from format.

4

Enforcement Mechanism

This group survives on enforcement.

Automatic Removal Rules

  • 2 consecutive missed submissions leads to removal.
  • 3 total misses, even if non-consecutive, leads to removal.
  • Repeated low-effort output leads to removal.
  • No engagement, including no comments or feedback, leads to removal.

No exceptions.

Definition of Low Effort

  • No meaningful progress since last submission.
  • Superficial updates that are cosmetic or trivial.
  • Recycled or old work.

Judgment call made by operator.

5

Membership Pipeline

Entry Requirements

  • Proof of recent work within 2 weeks.
  • Self-initiated work, not assigned work.
  • Clear demonstration of decision-making.

Screening Questions

  • What did you build recently?
  • What was hard about it?
  • What did you iterate on multiple times?

Reject fast if answers are vague.

6

Onboarding Protocol

Before Slack Invite

  • Review policy. Mandatory.
  • Submit initial work sample.

First Week

  • Must submit within first cycle.
  • Failure to submit leads to immediate removal.

Goal: filter early, not later.

7

Slack Structure

Channels

  • #build for submissions only.
  • #intro for onboarding only.
  • #random for everything else.

Rules

  • No discussions in #build beyond feedback.
  • No content dumping in #random.
  • No new channels without approval.

8

Feedback Standard

Feedback Must Be

  • Specific.
  • Actionable.
  • Direct.

Avoid

  • Praise without substance.
  • Generic comments.

Minimum: each member leaves at least 1 meaningful comment per week.

9

Operator Responsibilities

The group requires active enforcement.

  • Track weekly submissions.
  • Enforce removals without delay.
  • Maintain standard of output.
  • Admit new members selectively.

Failure here equals group collapse.

10

Failure Modes

  1. Activity decay. Fix with stricter enforcement.
  2. Quality dilution. Remove weakest contributors quickly.
  3. Overgrowth. Cap or slow admissions.
  4. Conversation drift. Redirect to output focus.

11

Growth Strategy

  • Start with 3-5 high-quality members.
  • Add slowly, one at a time.
  • Only admit if they raise the bar.

Do not optimize for size.

12

Culture

  • High accountability.
  • Low tolerance for excuses.
  • Respect through output.
  • Quiet intensity over loud participation.

13

Core Rule

If you are not building, you are removed. Everything else is secondary.

Read the rule set plainly. If the standard feels right, move to the join page and accept the invitation.
